name: flimanalyzer
description: Python package for analysis of Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) data.

readme.excerpt: # FLIMAnalyzer [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12%2B-blue)](https://github.com/uvaKCCI/flimanalyzer/blob/main/pyproject.toml) [![Tests](https://github.com/uvaKCCI/flimanalyzer/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/uvaKCCI/flimanalyzer/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/uvaKCCI/flimanalyzer/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/uvaKCCI/flimanalyzer) [![Documentation Status](https://readthedocs.org/projects/flimanalyzer/badge/?version=latest)](https://flimanalyzer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) [![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23426563.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23426563) Python package for analysis of Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) data. Documentation: https://flimanalyzer.readthedocs.io ## Requirements * Python 3.12 or later * All Python dependencies, including [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org) and [Prefect](https://www.prefect.io), are declared in `pyproject.toml` and installed automatically. ## Installation ### From PyPI with uv (recommended) [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) creates a virtual environment in `.venv` (installing a matching Python if needed). Then install FLIMAnalyzer with its graphical user interface (GUI) into it: uv venv --python 3.12 source .venv/bin/activate # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate uv pip install "flimanalyzer[gui]" The `gui` extra installs the GUI. Without it, `uv pip install flimanalyzer` installs only what [batch mode](#run-flimanalyzer-in-batch-mode) needs, for example on a computing cluster. Add `dask` for the optional Dask support (see [Concurrent and distributed execution](#concurrent-and-distributed-execution)), e.g. `"flimanalyzer[gui,dask]"`. ### From PyPI with pip python3.12 -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate pip install "flimanalyzer[gui]" ### PyTorch and the GPU Installed from PyPI, FLIMAnalyzer gets PyTorch from PyPI, which provides a different build on each platform: * **Linux:** the PyPI build includes CUDA, so an NVIDIA GPU is used if its driver is recent enough. * **Windows:** the PyPI build is CPU-only. For an NVIDIA GPU, install with `uv pip install "flimanalyzer[gui]" --torch-backend=cu128`, or with pip install the CUDA build first: `pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128`. See [pytorch.org](https://pytorch.org/get-started/locally/) for other CUDA versions. * **macOS:** only Apple Silicon is supported, because current PyTorch versions are not available for Intel Macs. The PyPI build uses the Apple GPU (MPS). ### Latest development version To install the current state of the repository, clone it and let uv create the environment. `uv sync` installs FLIMAnalyzer with the GUI in editable mode, with the exact package versions from `uv.lock` (the versions the tests run with). On Windows and Linux (x86_64), it installs the CUDA 12.8 build of PyTorch: git clone https://github.com/uvaKCCI/flimanalyzer.git cd flimanalyzer uv sync Without the GUI, with the test dependencies, or with Dask support: uv sync --no-group gui uv sync --extra test uv sync --extra dask With pip, in a virtual environment in the cloned folder: `pip install -e ".[gui]"`. ### With Docker The Docker images run only [batch mode](#run-flimanalyzer-in-batch-mode). They don't include the GUI. Each release is published to the GitHub Container Registry: | Image | | |---|---| | `ghcr.io/uvakcci/flimanalyzer:`, `:latest` | with the CUDA build of PyTorch (x86_64, several GB) | | `ghcr.io/uvakcci/flimanalyzer:-cpu`, `:latest-cpu` | CPU only (x86_64 and ARM), much smaller | docker pull ghcr.io/uvakcci/flimanalyzer:latest-cpu To build an image from the repository instead: with the CUDA 12.8 build of PyTorch, with the build for another CUDA version (here 12.6)
